items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: I would go out and look for jam sessions, and I would run in to guys like Harold West, Doc West, and Shadow Wilson, and Cozy Cole and Kaiser Marshall. I was competing with these kinds of people in jam sessions.

ctx.x: So, I stayed with Billy Hicks until around the latter part of May, I think it was, and I was in a jam session; you know, because during those days, I mean, every place -- the places to jam were all over, and that's why the unions stopped jamming, because the nightclub operators used to hire like a piano and a drummer, and they'd start at nine o'clock, and nine thirty, you had a whole band up on the stage for free. So that's why the unions stopped jam sessions.

But I used to make every jam -- you know, after I came to New York and found out that I was able to play, even to this day, I am still competitive -- I am very competitive, and I would go out and look for jam sessions, and I would run in to guys like Harold West, Doc West, and Shadow Wilson, and Cozy Cole and Kaiser Marshall. I was competing with these kinds of people in jam sessions. So as fate would have it, I was at a jam session one night, and Roy came in. And they were playing at the Arcadia Ballroom.
